name: Decimal._isinfinity

name: Decimal._check_nans
note: review: ComparisonsConsistent uses only the no-NaN case and `isSome` for a quiet NaN on the left; the sNaN branches (:810-815, InvalidOperation then the quieted operand), their precedence over quiet NaNs, and the NaN value returned are never stated.

name: Decimal._compare_check_nans
note: review: Only a left quiet NaN with no sNaN is stated (flag set, `<` false); the docstring's point, sNaN taking precedence over qNaN on either side (:837-852), and the NaN returned are unstated, so an order-insensitive check passes.

name: Decimal.__bool__

name: Decimal._cmp
note: review: No theorem relates cmpVal to the numeric values: ComparisonsConsistent states only antisymmetry and CompareTotalOrder only zero-iff-identical, so a reversed _cmp (and with it reversed <, max, min) passes both; citation :862-924 includes the comment block after the function (:909-924).

name: Decimal.__eq__
note: review: _convert_for_comparison (:927; int, float, Rational, complex operands and NotImplemented) is not modelled, the result is pinned only to the unpinned _cmp, and the sNaN case (InvalidOperation, then False) is unstated.

name: Decimal.__lt__
note: review: _convert_for_comparison (:935) is not modelled; `<` is stated as `cmpVal a b = .lt`, i.e. pinned only to _cmp, which is unpinned (a reversed _cmp passes), and the sNaN and right-hand NaN cases are unstated.

name: Decimal.__le__

name: Decimal.__gt__

name: Decimal.__ge__
note: review: _convert_for_comparison (:962) is not modelled; `>=` is pinned only to the unpinned _cmp and no NaN case is stated for it.

name: Decimal.compare
note: review: compareD mirrors :978-986 but the property pins it only to `decOfInt (cmpInt a b)`, i.e. to the unpinned _cmp, and the NaN branch (:981-984: the NaN returned, sNaN signalling) is not stated.

name: Decimal.__hash__
note: review: The only entry is the int-limit refutation (hash(Decimal(10**4300))), a limitation upstream declined (python/cpython#96589; the record says do not file), so it is not a promised behaviour; nothing states the hash of an in-limit value (no narrowed twin agreement or Fraction-consistency for _pydecimal).

name: Decimal.__add__
note: review: `add` (Arith.lean:421) mirrors :1207-1286, but the only settled entries are the int-limit refutations (deliberate per python/cpython#96589, record kind known-limitation), and decimal-add-correct is open, so nothing pins the sum for in-limit operands: an __add__ returning any value below 4300 digits passes.

name: Decimal.__sub__
note: review: `sub` mirrors :1292-1302, but the only settled entry is the int-limit refutation (declined upstream); decimal-sub-correct is open, so the difference is unpinned.

name: Decimal.__mul__
note: review: MulCorrect holds only when `*` returns (an always-raising __mul__ satisfies it, and nothing states when it returns) and assumes the subnormal and overflow ranges away (decimal-mul-subnormal-correct, -overflow-correct open); the other entry is the declined int-limit refutation.

name: Decimal.__truediv__
note: review: TruedivSpecials pins the zero/infinity cases, but TruedivCoreCorrect is conditional on truedivFin returning and stops before _fix (the correctly rounded quotient is unstated), so a __truediv__ raising for every finite non-zero pair passes; 0/x and NaN operands are not stated.

name: Decimal._divide
note: review: divideD mirrors :1434-1464, but DivideVerdict holds only when _divide returns (an always-raising _divide passes) and names the helper's decision instead of q < 10**prec (DivideCorrect open, and per its note false at prec 727115501); the floordiv refutation runs _divide but the defect it shows is __floordiv__'s missing _fix.

name: Decimal.__divmod__
note: review: DivmodConsistent is the finite-path body unfolded by `rfl` (divmodD = divideD then _fix of the remainder); the special branches (:1484-1503: NaNs, INF with InvalidOperation, x/0 giving DivisionByZero plus InvalidOperation, 0/0 DivisionUndefined) are unstated, and the twin disagreement recorded for its quotient (decimal-pydecimal-floordiv-no-finalize) is not an entry of this row.

name: Decimal.__mod__
note: review: DivmodConsistent is `rfl` on the finite path (modD = _fix of _divide's remainder); 'INF % x' and 'x % 0' InvalidOperation, '0 % 0' DivisionUndefined and the NaN branch (:1527-1537) are unstated, and _divide itself is pinned only conditionally.

name: Decimal._fix
note: review: `fix` mirrors :1723-1803 branch by branch, but MulCorrect and QuantizeCorrect hold only when the operation returns (an always-raising _fix passes) and assume the Overflow (:1747-1752, :1774-1775), Underflow/Subnormal and Clamped-on-underflow branches away; those are the open decimal-mul-overflow-correct and -subnormal-correct.

name: Decimal.__round__
note: review: IntConversionsPyOrLimit's `∨ ∃ msg, ValueError` is unconstrained, so a round() that always raises ValueError passes; the other entries are the declined int-limit refutation and QuantizeCorrect, which holds only when quantize returns; the n-argument TypeError (:1932-1933) is not modelled.

name: Decimal.__floor__
note: review: pyToInt .floor mirrors :1953-1958, but IntConversionsPyOrLimit allows any ValueError (an always-raising floor passes) and the other entry is the declined int-limit refutation; nothing bounds the ValueError to results past 4300 digits.

name: Decimal.__ceil__
note: review: Same as __floor__: IntConversionsPyOrLimit's unconstrained ValueError disjunct is met by an always-raising ceil, and the refutation is the declined int limit.

name: Decimal.quantize
note: review: quantize/quantizeFin (Arith.lean:257-281) mirror :2605-2659 and QuantizeCorrect is a strong statement, but it holds only when quantize returns, so an always-raising quantize passes, and the special operands (:2612-2621: NaNs, both-infinite returns self, one INF gives InvalidOperation) are not stated.

name: Decimal._rescale
note: review: `rescale` mirrors :2687-2708, but RoundingModesCorrect's `∨ ∃ msg, ValueError` is unconstrained, so a _rescale that always raises ValueError passes; the zero and padding branches are stated only through QuantizeCorrect, which is conditional on returning.

name: Decimal.to_integral_exact
note: review: ToIntegralExactCorrect holds only when to_integral_exact returns (an always-raising one passes) and covers only finite non-zero values with exp < 0; the special, exp >= 0 and zero branches (:2743-2751) are not stated.

name: Decimal.to_integral_value
note: review: ToIntegralValueCorrect pins exp >= 0 unconditionally, but for exp < 0 its `∨ ∃ msg, ValueError` is unconstrained (an always-raising rounding branch passes), and the NaN/infinity branch (:2768-2772) and zero coefficient are unstated.

name: Decimal.max

name: Decimal.min

name: Decimal.adjusted

name: Decimal.compare_signal
note: review: compareSignal mirrors :2993-2997, but only the no-NaN case is stated (equal to compare, i.e. the unpinned _cmp); the branch the method exists for, every NaN signalling with sNaN first, is unstated.

name: Decimal.compare_total
note: review: compareTotal mirrors :3006-3069, but CompareTotalOrder states only antisymmetry and zero-iff-identical: the negation of the correct order, or any antisymmetric injective ranking, passes; transitivity, agreement with numeric order and the documented NaN placement are unstated.

name: Decimal.compare_total_mag
note: review: CopyOpsCorrect restates the definition `compareTotalMag a b = compareTotal (copyAbs a) (copyAbs b)` by `rfl` plus reflexivity and antisymmetry, inheriting compare_total's unpinned order.

name: Decimal.copy_abs
note: review: CopyOpsCorrect states only that copy_abs's sign is 0 and that it is idempotent (and absorbs copy_sign): a constant Decimal('0') satisfies all three, so the magnitude is unpinned.

name: Decimal.copy_negate
note: review: CopyOpsCorrect states only an involution that flips the sign, which `±c·10^e ↦ ∓c·10^-e` also satisfies; copyAbs (copyNegate a) = copyAbs a is not stated, and the other entry is the declined int-limit refutation.

name: Decimal.is_canonical

name: Decimal.is_normal
note: review: ClassificationCorrect states only `is_normal != is_subnormal` on finite non-zero values: the Emin threshold is never stated (any threshold shared with is_subnormal passes) and False for zeros and specials (:3202-3203) is unstated.

name: Decimal.is_subnormal
note: review: Only the exclusive-or with is_normal on finite non-zero values is stated; the `adjusted() < Emin` threshold and False for zeros and specials are unstated.

name: Decimal.is_zero
note: review: is_zero appears only in `decBool d = !isZero d`, true by definition; no statement says it is true exactly for a zero coefficient, so is_zero ≡ False with __bool__ ≡ True passes.

name: Decimal.max_mag
note: review: MinMaxCorrect states only operand-order independence for max_mag: which operand wins is never stated (min_mag ≡ max_mag passes), nor any NaN case (:3522-3532).

name: Decimal.min_mag
note: review: Only operand-order independence is stated, so a min_mag returning the larger magnitude passes; no NaN case is stated.

name: Decimal.number_class
